subject: Post-call performance checklist & replay requests
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@sablehealth.com>, Arjun Singh <arjun@cloudops.sablehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T14:22:00Z
Subject: Post-call performance checklist & replay requests

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope a focused performance qualification. High-level notes from the call:
- Sable Health production targets: p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 500 ms (end-to-end, including network hop to provider).
- Current provider (they shared sample): observed p95 ~ 320 ms, p99 spikes to ~720 ms during bursts and cold starts.
- Important traffic characteristics: short prompt lengths (avg 240 tokens), 10% streaming responses (progressive chunking), peak concurrency windows around 09:00–11:00 PT (regional), baseline steady qps ~ 40 with 10x short bursts.

As discussed, our immediate asks to scope a deterministic replay and performance probe:
1) Sable to share a 1-hour anonymized traffic sample (already uploaded per Maya — s3 link in related_links).
2) Perm for Redwood to run a staging replay against a hosted test token (non-prod) with identical request envelope (headers, chunking behavior).
3) Define pass/fail thresholds: p95 < 150 ms; p99 < 500 ms; no more than 1% request failures under 1.5x peak concurrency.
4) Confirm whether prefix caching/warm-up is permitted (recommend enabling for replay to measure warm vs cold tails).

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Today: confirm replay window and token provisioning (owner: Maya).
- +48 hours: Redwood runs baseline synthetic replay (owner: Lukas) and shares raw timing CSV + summary.
- +5 business days: controlled POC with live traffic shadowing (if agreed) or extended replay to validate fallbacks and streaming chunk behaviors.

Attach: call recording + incumbent latency sample (attached).

Next steps (please confirm):
- Maya: confirm example hour and give staging token permissions OR provide a redacted sample if token not allowed.
- Arjun: any network egress constraints we should be aware of (IP allowlist, MTU limits).
- Marissa / Ben / Karthik: internal owners for replay, kernel selection, and streaming-test config.

Thanks — Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@sablehealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Singh <arjun@cloudops.sablehealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call performance checklist & replay requests

Thanks, Lukas — great recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirming the sample is at s3://sable-health-poc/traffic-sample-202803.zip (we redacted PII and replaced user IDs).
- Incumbent numbers are aggregated from last week's production window: typical p95 320 ms, p99 700–750 ms on peak — cold-starts during deploys push p99 above 1s briefly.
- Streaming model behavior: we stream every chunk of generated text; typical response is 3–6 chunks depending on the prompt. Latency sensitivity is highest for the UI flows where we stream early tokens.
- We can grant a staging API key restricted to non-prod with an allowlist for Redwood IPs. Please provide the list of IPs you will use for the controlled replay.

Questions for Redwood:
1) When you say "prefix caching/warm-up" — will that be part of the default hosted probe or a separate warm-up run? We want both cold and warm numbers.
2) For streaming tests, can you replicate chunked delivery (first-chunk < 100ms ideally) while keeping overall p99 under 500ms?

We can sign the standard NDA (link provided) and give the sample access as soon as the allowlist is in place.

—Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Product, Sable Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@sablehealth.com>, Arjun Singh <arjun@cloudops.sablehealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call performance checklist & replay requests

Looping in the perf team owners and proposing a concrete execution checklist. Quick notes and owners: 
- IP allowlist & token handling (owner: Ben) — Ben, please confirm the Redwood test egress IPs and whether we need to allocate dedicated infra for this probe.
- Replay harness & measurement (owner: Karthik) — plan: run three phases: cold-run (no warm-up), warm-run (prefix cache populated for 15 minutes), and burst-run (2x peak concurrency sustained for 10 minutes). Output: per-request timestamped CSV and aggregated p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end and server-only.
- Streaming chunk fidelity (owner: Lukas) — we will emulate the client's chunking pattern (3–6 chunks) and measure first-chunk latency independently.
- Failover behavior: include a fallback run where we exercise a smaller quantized model variant to check graceful degradation p99.

Proposed test config (initial):
- Target concurrency envelope: steady 40 qps, 10s bursts ramping to 400 concurrent warm requests (this models their 10x spike).
- Batching: test with continuous-batching off and on (max batch size 8) to show trade-offs.
- Observability hooks: we will include token-level latency metadata and trace IDs for correlation.

Deliverables and ETA:
- Raw CSVs and summary report within 48h of token + allowlist (deliverable owner: Karthik).
- One-page executive summary comparing Redwood hosted vs incumbent numbers (deliverable owner: Marissa) within 72h.
- Recommendation: if p99 remains above 500ms in warm-run, propose a Dedicated capacity pilot to further tune kernel selection and placement.

Marissa
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Arjun Singh <arjun@cloudops.sablehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@sablehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call performance checklist & replay requests

Ben — sending allowlist and temporary staging token details in a separate secure channel (per our security policy). We also uploaded an additional 30-minute sample showing peak bursts (s3://sable-health-poc/traffic-peak-202804.zip).

We signed the NDA via DocuSign (link above). Please confirm once Redwood confirms IPs so we can flip the allowlist. Looking forward to the replay and the CSVs for our observability.

Thanks,
Arjun Singh
Head of Cloud Engineering, Sable Health
